primary_source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon, 1999)
policy: Source annotations only; do not overwrite species records, range statuses, source credits or live gallery

morphology.habit: Freely branched erect annual to 50 cm
morphology.leaves: Long petioles; nearly glabrous blade 1.5–5.3 cm wide; ovate, slightly cordate base per key
morphology.inflorescence: Pistillate spikes terminal, staminate spikes axillary; apetalous unisexual flowers
morphology.fruits: Three-carpellate capsule; detailed measurement not in historical species paragraph
morphology.habitat: Stream banks and bottoms, disturbed areas and roadsides

records.diagnosis: Unlike A. phleoides, separate male and female spikes; unlike dioecious A. radians, both on same annual individual
records.caveat: A. persimilis vs A. ostryifolia nomenclature remains contested; modern concept crosswalk must be retained, not represented as identical type
records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon, 1999)

morphology.habit: Perennial, branched multiple stems from woody root, spreading to erect, to 60 cm long
morphology.stems: Long spreading pilose hairs, curled short hairs, or glabrous
morphology.leaves: Lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, evenly sharply toothed
morphology.inflorescence: Terminal bisexual spikes, male and female parts within same spike per key; styles conspicuously reddish

records.diagnosis: Woody-rooted perennial with terminal mixed reproductive spikes vs annual A. persimilis
records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon, 1999)

morphology.stems: Densely short stiff and long-spreading hairy
morphology.leaves: Reniform to orbicular, 8–12 mm wide; petioles 4–16 mm usually as long as or longer than blades
morphology.inflorescence: Dioecious per 1999 genus key; pistillate bracts 3.5–10 mm, 7–13 lobes

records.diagnosis: Small radiating divided leaves and male/female plants separate; contrast monoecious A. phleoides
records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon, 1999)

alternative.source: PlantNET New South Wales Flora Online; Kew POWO

morphology.habit: Erect shrub to 60 cm, rigid angular branches sometimes almost leafless
morphology.flowers: Usually monoecious according to PlantNET (not reliably dioecious as existing learner field states)
morphology.other: Australian-native genus and species, not North American native

records.caveat: Not in 1999 flora; existing learner says usually dioecious while PlantNET says usually monoecious. Hold sex expression for revision; no Texas BONAP native claim
records.source: Alternate named authority; 1999 species account not located

morphology.leaves: Elliptic to ovate, sessile above, prominent veins below
morphology.inflorescence: Usually dioecious; axillary racemes longer than leaves per genus key
morphology.flowers: Male petals obovate/cuneate ca. 4–5 mm, truncate glands wider than long, 8–10 stamens; female petals rudimentary/absent, glands square and thick, styles erect bifid for half free length
morphology.fruit: Three-seeded capsule at genus level, exact measurements not in 1999 account
morphology.habitat: Sandy or rocky limestone soils, Edwards Plateau

records.diagnosis: Long racemes + conspicuously truncate squarish floral glands vs linear glands of D. humilis or D. mercurialina
records.caveat: 1999 specifically says current populations not known from Hays despite older citation; never interpret historical Hays entry as current confirmed occurrence
records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon, 1999)

records.flora_name: Ditaxis humilis (Engelm. & A.Gray) Pax var. humilis

morphology.leaves: Elliptic to narrowly obovate, villous to variable, upper leaves sessile or nearly; lower veins conspicuous
morphology.inflorescence: Monoecious, short axillary racemes less than subtending leaves
morphology.flowers: Male petals narrow lanceolate/oblanceolate; glands linear; 8–9 stamens; pistillate petals absent or to 0.5 mm, styles bifid
morphology.fruit: Three-seeded capsules; seed surfaces may be rugose vs nearly smooth variants

historical_synonyms: Argythamnia humilis var. leiosperma Waterfall (historical infraspecific concept)
records.diagnosis: Short raceme and spreading many-branch habit vs upright longer-racemed A. aphoroides
records.caveat: 1999 variety concepts humilis, leiosperma, laevis have unresolved taxonomic inclusion at broader accepted species level
records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon, 1999)

alternative.source: Flora of North America Argythamnia simulans

morphology.habit: Perennial or low subshrub (existing FNA-backed specimen profile)
morphology.flowers: Staminate sepals 4–5.3 mm, petals 2–4 mm; 7–8 stamens, no staminodes; pistillate sepals 6–9 mm, styles 1.5–2.1 mm
morphology.fruit: Hispidulous capsules 3.5–9 mm; seeds 3.5–4.2 mm slightly irregular alveolate

records.diagnosis: Sessile leaves, fairly long bisexual racemes, 7–8 stamens distinguish from A. aphoroides and A. humilis
records.caveat: Absent from located 1999 flora treatment; ITIS accepts Ditaxis simulans while Kew accepts Argythamnia simulans; retain taxon concept dispute
records.source: Alternate named authority; 1999 species account not located

alternative.source: Flora of North America Bernardia myricifolia

morphology.habit: Shrub up to about 3 m (FNA-backed repository research)
morphology.leaves: Broad elliptic to nearly round, revolute crenate edge, underside densely gray-white stellate hairy
morphology.flowers: Dioecious; staminate inflorescence 5–15 mm, typically 12–15 stamens; pistil three-carpellate with densely brush-haired stigmatic styles

records.diagnosis: Stellate leaf underside with dioecious flowers and three-carpellate fruit; distinguish other Bernardia via stipule resin, stamen number and carpels
records.caveat: Not found as named species in extracted 1999 flora; FNA indicates mostly southern Texas range, not BONAP county proof
records.source: Alternate named authority; 1999 species account not located

morphology.habit: Milky-sapped perennial up to 80(–100) cm with deep thick branching root to 20 cm
morphology.stems: Dense extremely painful pale stinging hairs, leaves less densely hispid
morphology.leaves: Alternate, long petioles, blades 6–15 cm wide, cordate, palmately 3–5 deeply lobed, coarsely toothed
morphology.flowers: Showy fragrant white inflorescence terminal, cymose, both sexes present; male perianth tube 15–20 mm, (4–)5 lobes; female perianth 10–17 mm, deeply 5-parted
morphology.fruit: Hispid capsules 15–20 mm with three large seeds 14–18 mm
morphology.habitat: Open sandy woods, fields, disturbed ground

records.diagnosis: Stinging hairs + large palmately lobed leaves and white flowers; contrast non-stinging peltate Ricinus communis
records.caveat: Risk of painful contact; no field handling recommended
records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon, 1999)

morphology.leaves: Alternate; tip acute to obtuse; hairs stellate, leaves often ovate/lance-elliptic
morphology.flowers: Terminal spike-like racemes; three styles divided repeatedly
morphology.fruit: Three-seeded capsule; 1999 Croton key says styles ultimate branches ca. 10+, pistillate sepals 5–10 mm
morphology.habitat: Sandy or calcareous prairies, pastures, roadsides

records.diagnosis: Historical var. capitatus: middle and upper petioles similar length, leaves often blunt, uniform seed color; var. lindheimeri: petioles shorten upward, more pointed leaves, mottled seeds
records.caveat: Check C. lindheimeri / C. lindheimerianus separate repository concepts before assigning varieties
records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon, 1999)
